не трать время (прямой совет) · or: Don't waste your time. (резче)

blocks.instr: Which situation fits the phrase, a or b? Why not the other one? Then tap the card.
blocks.tip: Say a or b and why. Tap to check. ↺ Again later = we weren't sure: the card comes back two or three cards later.

cards.front:
It really **picks up**.
a) The first episodes are slow, but then it gets exciting.
b) It starts brilliantly, but then it gets boring.
cards.back: **a** — it gets better and more interesting

cards.front:
I just **couldn't get into** it.
a) The cinema was full, so we couldn't get in.
b) I watched two episodes, but it didn't grab me.
cards.back: **b** — it didn't interest me, so I stopped

cards.front:
All the **hype put me off**.
a) Everyone said it was a masterpiece, so I didn't want to watch it.
b) The music was so loud that I switched it off.
cards.back: **a** — all the excitement made me not want to watch it

cards.front:
Some of the jokes **haven't aged well**.
a) The actors look much older now.
b) An old comedy has jokes that feel wrong or awkward today.
cards.back: **b** — about how something feels now, not how people look

cards.front:
It **takes me back**.
a) A film from your childhood reminds you of Sunday evenings with your family.
b) You take a DVD back to the library.
cards.back: **a** — it brings back memories

cards.front:
…, **I'll give it that**.
a) You give your friend a DVD as a present.
b) You didn't like the film, but you admit the music was great.
cards.back: **b** — you admit one good thing

cards.front:
I **see** it **in a different light** now.
a) You watched it again on a bigger, brighter TV.
b) You rewatched it as an adult and now you understand the parents.
cards.back: **b** — you understand it differently now

cards.front:
**Is it any good?**
a) You want a friend's opinion of a series before you watch it.
b) You want to know if the series is suitable for children.
cards.back: **a** — a question about quality

cards.front:
Honestly? **I wouldn't bother.**
a) A noise outside doesn't disturb you.
b) A friend asks if a film is worth watching, and you found it boring.
cards.back: **b** — it's not worth your time

blocks.instr: Our sentences. With a finished time it's past simple — in both. How would you say the grey part?

cards.front: ~~Have you seen~~ the Star Kitchen final ^^yesterday^^?
cards.back: **Did you see** the Star Kitchen final yesterday?

cards.front: ^^When^^ ~~have you heard~~ about it?
cards.back: When **did you hear** about it?

cards.front: ~~Have you cried~~ ^^when you watched it^^?
cards.back: **Did you cry** when you watched it?

blocks.instr: Our sentences. Green = good, grey = could be better. How would you make it perfect English?

cards.front: Do you think so? I found it a bit boring. Maybe all <g>the hype</g> ~~affect me negatively~~.
cards.back: Maybe all the hype **spoiled it for me**.
cards.why: Hype — отличное слово! Spoiled it for me — испортило удовольствие. Put me off — оттолкнуло, отбило желание смотреть.

cards.ctx: пересмотрела — и теперь вижу фильм по-другому
cards.front: So now I ~~watch this film with another eyes~~.
cards.back: So now I **see this film in a different light**.
cards.why: With another eyes здесь не подходит. Наш вариант: I see it in a different light now.

cards.ctx: фильм из детства — пересматриваешь, и как будто снова там
cards.front: You can just enjoy it because ~~you can get back to~~ <g>your childhood</g>.
cards.back: You can just enjoy it because **it takes you back to** your childhood.
cards.why: It takes me back (to…) — возвращает в прошлое.

cards.ctx: не смотрела — спрашиваешь, смотреть или нет
cards.front: <g>I haven't, actually.</g> ~~Maybe should I see that or no~~?
cards.back: I haven't, actually. **Should I watch it?** / **Is it any good?**
cards.why: I haven't, actually — отлично! В вопросе should — на первом месте, а or no не нужно. «Стоит смотреть?» обычно спрашивают так: Is it any good?

blocks.instr: What have you been watching or reading? Recommend or warn your partner off. Use the box.
items: **1**  Get ready (1 min): think of something you'd recommend, something you gave up on or wouldn't bother with, and an old favourite — has it aged well?
**2**  In pairs: Have you seen / read …? Is it any good? Recommend it or warn your partner off. Follow up on what your partner says.
**3**  Which is the worst: a slow start, a disappointing ending, or jokes that haven't aged well? Give a reason for each.
**4**  Think of a series you gave up on — or a popular one lots of people give up on. Give two reasons why it's hard to get into. Is it worth a second try?
blocks.fast: If you're done: go back to 📖 Text & new phrases and say the missing words without looking. Then tell your partner what you'll give a try — and what you'll skip.

blocks.instr: Recommending: what we often say → what people usually say. How would you say it?

cards.front: I recommend ~~to watch~~ it with subtitles.
cards.back: I recommend **watching** it with subtitles.

cards.front: I strongly recommend ~~to see~~.
cards.back: I strongly recommend **it**.

cards.front: I definitely recommend ~~this for you~~.
cards.back: I definitely recommend **it**.

cards.front: I honestly ~~suggest you to~~ give this series a try.
cards.back: I honestly **think you should** give this series a try.
cards.why: suggest you to — так не говорят.

cards.front: So you ~~don't recommend to read~~ it?
cards.back: So you **wouldn't** recommend it?

cards.front: It's not really my thing. I would not recommend ~~you to watch~~ it.
cards.back: It's not really my thing. I would not recommend it. / Honestly? **I wouldn't bother.**
cards.why: recommend sb to do — редко и звучит официально.
